claims.text: As-cast equimolar HfNbTaTiZr is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Equimolar HfNbTaTiZr has a distorted BCC lattice with large lattice misfits.
Large atomic-size and modulus mismatches produce severe solid-solution strengthening.
Short-range-order clusters form in HfNbTaTiZr and help control its elevated-temperature response.
Lattice distortion and short-range order synergistically raise the Peierls barrier and dynamically pin dislocations.
The proposed lattice-friction and pinning mechanism causes higher-than-expected yield strength in the 873–1073 K range.
The proposed mechanism alters stress–strain behavior in the 873–1073 K range.
The proposed mechanism produces nonlinear thermal-expansion trends in the 873–1073 K range.
Partially replacing Hf with a closer-in-size element would reduce lattice distortion.
Thermal activation at elevated temperatures facilitates the formation and evolution of short-range-order clusters.
Short-range-order clusters impede dislocation glide.
The combined effects of lattice distortion and short-range order slow the temperature-induced loss of yield strength.
The combined effects of lattice distortion and short-range order slow the temperature-induced loss of elastic modulus.
HfNbTaTiZr should retain more yield strength than the reduced-distortion variant.
HfNbTaTiZr should show an anomalous plateau or reduced strain-hardening rate between 873 and 1073 K relative to the reduced-distortion variant.
HfNbTaTiZr should show a distinct temperature dependence of elastic modulus relative to the reduced-distortion variant.
HfNbTaTiZr should show a distinct temperature dependence of thermal-expansion coefficient relative to the reduced-distortion variant.
More pronounced short-range-order or clustering features should be observed in standard HfNbTaTiZr than in the reduced-distortion variant.
The compositionally modified variant is expected to exhibit a more conventional BCC thermomechanical response.
The mechanism is expected to apply to single-phase equimolar BCC HEAs up to approximately 1200 K, provided phase transformations, grain-boundary effects, and oxidation do not dominate.

contradictions.description: The proposed comparator partially substitutes Hf and therefore is not the stated equimolar five-component HfNbTaTiZr composition, while the baseline still calls it a variant of HfNbTaTiZr and the boundary restricts the hypothesis to equimolar HEAs.
